items.label: Mode 50
items.note: Forty-five notes of the piano are prepared, producing a range of small percussion sounds. Vandré plays a Steinway O; the label’s account explains how the instrument’s string lengths affect the preparations. The work consists of sixteen sonatas and four interludes.

items.label: Mode 147
items.note: Cage’s chance operations produced four books of precisely written piano music, made up of sharp attacks, silences and sounds made inside the instrument. Joste’s recording places them between Seven Haiku and the Suite for Toy Piano.

items.recorded: June 2011, Boutell Memorial Concert Hall, Northern Illinois University, DeKalb
items.label: Mode 243
items.note: Four percussionists play different phrase patterns within the same twenty-four-bar spans. Tin cans, rattles, drums and conch shell take turns. Third Coast’s recording couples the piece with the other two Constructions; the filmed edition shows the exchanges between the players.

items.performers: Essential Music; John Kennedy and Charles Wood, directors
items.label: Mode 239
items.note: Essential Music plays Five by blowing into bottles, an instrumental choice Cage approved. Seven and Thirteen expand the group. These late works allow players to place their sounds within specified time-brackets, and sustained notes overlap without a conductor coordinating their entries.
